title: Multi-format scheduled delivery with verification and tenant-aware backpressure
creator: Aisha Mehta
description:
Summary:
Build a resilient, tenant-aware scheduled export delivery flow that supports CSV and Parquet, direct S3 uploads (signed/multipart), and webhook fanout with deterministic verification. This scope focuses on correctness and observability for scheduled tenant exports (daily/weekly), while enabling consumers to validate delivery and handle duplicates via an idempotency contract.

Goals:
- Deliver scheduled exports reliably to S3 or customer webhooks with clear delivery semantics (at-least-once with idempotency tokens).
- Support multi-format payloads: line-delimited CSV for legacy consumers and partitioned Parquet for analytics consumers.
- Provide verification artifacts (manifest + checksums) so customers and internal jobs can assert correctness before ingestion.
- Apply tenant-aware backpressure and configurable retry policies to avoid noisy neighbor effects.
- Ship comprehensive metrics, alerts, and a runbook for delivery failures and remediation.

Success metrics (first 90 days):
- 99.95% scheduled-export delivery rate to primary targets (S3 signed URL or webhook 2xx).
- Mean time to detect failed export < 5 minutes (alerting/observability).
- Customer-visible schema change rollouts with zero-breaking changes for 95% of tenants.
- Reduction in manual re-delivery requests by 80% vs baseline.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- Format and storage: We'll generate both CSV and Parquet where enabled to avoid forcing all consumers to migrate. Parquet production requires batching and a small staging ECS job per tenant to write Avro/Parquet; this adds compute cost but improves downstream query performance.
- Idempotency and dedup: Each export will publish a manifest JSON with a stable export_id and per-file checksums (sha256). For webhook delivery we include an X-Redwood-Export header with export_id and an idempotency key. Receivers should use these to deduplicate. Internal replays use the manifest to validate completeness.
- Delivery semantics: Default is at-least-once. We will offer an optional at-most-once toggle for webhook destinations that explicitly request it (customers accept potential data loss).
- Backpressure: implement a tenant token-bucket rate limiter and per-tenant concurrency limit. If a tenant exceeds capacity or an endpoint returns sustained 5xx, we escalate to a backoff queue with exponential jitter and move to a low-priority retry lane. This avoids global queue clogging.
- Streaming vs batch: Small exports (<100 MB) will be single-part uploads. Larger exports use S3 multipart with pre-signed URLs; we will publish the multipart manifest and finalize only after all parts uploaded. This supports resumable downloads and improves upload success for flaky connections.
- Encryption & signing: All artifacts to S3 must use SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS per tenant preference. Webhook payloads support HMAC signature header for authenticity (docs to be added).

Schema & compatibility:
- Introduce a schema_version string in every manifest and file-level metadata. Schema changes must be additive. Non-additive changes require a migration flag and a staged rollout: canary -> broad -> opt-in.
- Provide a lightweight compatibility checker service (schema-lint) that runs against sample export manifests on PRs to prevent accidental breaking changes.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flagged backend: implement for CSV-only to validate control flow and metrics in staging (2 sprints).
2) Parquet path: introduce background converter worker and storage partitioning (2 sprints).
3) Webhook improvements: HMAC signatures + idempotency headers + backoff lanes (1 sprint).
4) Customer beta: onboard 3 willing customers to exercise manifests, presigned uploads, and dedupe flow (2 weeks).
5) GA: release to all customers with default conservative retry/backoff settings and choice to opt-in to aggressive throughput.

Observability & runbooks:
- Metrics: per-tenant export_success_rate, export_latency_ms, webhook_2xx_rate, s3_signed_url_expiry_failures, manifest_checksum_mismatch_count.
- Traces: instrument end-to-end trace id on export requests and include step spans: prepare -> write -> multipart finalize -> manifest publish -> delivery fanout -> ack.
- Alerts: export_success_rate < 99.5% over 15m (P0); manifest_checksum_mismatch_count > 0 for > 5 tenants in 1h (P1).
- Runbook: include steps for resending a manifest, forcing reprocessing from storage, rotating webhook secrets, and escalating to on-call infra for storage permission issues.

Testing & validation:
- Integration tests to simulate S3 presigned multipart uploads, slow webhook endpoints, and duplicate deliveries.
- Chaos tests: random S3 signaling failures and transient 5xx from webhook endpoints to validate retry/backoff lanes.
- Canary gating with shadow deliveries to a subset of internal tenants to validate manifests and checksums without impacting customer targets.

Open questions / outstanding tasks:
- Do we need per-tenant configurable retention for signed URLs beyond 24 hours? (PM wants 7-day option for slow customers).
- SLA implications for the at-most-once toggle: legal and support need to weigh in.
- Final decision on default Parquet partitioning schema and time-bucketing granularity.

References & artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Export+Schemas+and+Versioning
- Implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1298
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/exports/exports-delivery-overview

Next steps (owner: Daniel Park):
- Implement manifest generation and publish to exports-metadata topic (Kafka).
- Wire up S3 multipart presigned URL flow and write finalizer lambda.
- Add the webhook idempotency headers to the delivery worker and implement token-bucket per-tenant limiter.
- Add observability metrics and alerting rules in Grafana/Prometheus.
